correctness.rationale: The final newly seen symbols of successive greedy complete arches form a test subsequence whose earliest embedding reaches the arch boundaries; appending a letter missing in the remainder proves the greedy index bound, including no complete arches. For the palindrome, the same terminal-symbol test from both ends forces any inserted middle test word to embed in the reflected remainder with or without the center. That core has index zero when it misses a letter and otherwise index one: in the latter case the center is the sole occurrence of the letter missing from the half-remainder, so a double of that letter is absent. Concatenating the complete arches and using this core proves the quoted index rule in all cases. First-appearance orders give the displayed A_q and R_{q,j} factors (allow repetitions between discoveries and, for remainders only, after the last discovery). For q-1 remainder symbols precisely one center contributes u instead of 1 in the residual weight. The minimum m for 2h even index is qh and yields (q!)^h half-words; for 2h+1 odd index the minimum half-length is qh+q-1 with forced center and (q!)^(h+1) choices. The candidate minima increase strictly with k, so the at-least-k formulation gives the same extremals. Under uniform sampling of the half, the iid arch intervals are coupon-collector times with the stated mean and variance and exponential tails. The finite-moment renewal mean, variance and inverse-sum CLT apply; doubling N(floor(n/2)) multiplies its variance by four, and an extra term in [0,1] changes variance by at most O(sqrt(n)) and does not change the scaled limit. At q=2 this gives 4/27. The supplied exhaustive finite checker and its recorded scope were inspected, not run; the independent arch and renewal argument settles the general claim. No uniformity in growing q is established.
